title.en: What is inside a toothpaste and a train?

text.en: A bright smile from toothpaste, the rail track under a train and the electricity in your house all depend on minerals. Today we find where India gets them.

A mineral is a homogenous naturally occurring substance with a definable internal structure. Minerals are found in ores.
Minerals occur in igneous and metamorphic rocks as veins and lodes, in sedimentary rocks in layers, as alluvial deposits called placers, and in ocean waters.
Minerals are classified as ferrous (iron, manganese), non-ferrous (copper, bauxite, lead, zinc, tin) and non-metallic (mica, limestone).
Iron ore is the backbone of industry. The main belts are Odisha-Jharkhand, Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur, Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru and Maharashtra-Goa.
Energy resources are conventional such as coal, petroleum, natural gas and electricity, and non-conventional such as solar, wind, tidal and biogas.
Coal is the most abundant fossil fuel in India. Petroleum comes mainly from Mumbai High and Assam, and natural gas from the Krishna-Godavari basin.
Hydroelectricity and thermal power are the main sources of electricity. Tamil Nadu is a leader in wind energy near Nagercoil and Madurai (additional, not in the textbook).
We must conserve minerals and energy because they are finite resources, by using them carefully, recycling and using renewable sources.

problem.en: A power plant burns 5,000 tonnes of coal per day. How much in 30 days?

why.en: Large numbers show why saving matters.

requiredIdeas.en: They are finite and take millions of years to form
Use carefully, recycle and use renewables

points.en: Minerals occur in ores in rocks and alluvial deposits.
They are ferrous, non-ferrous or non-metallic.
